text: Good API design is essential for creating software that is easy to use and maintain. When building REST APIs, the first step is to define clear, logical endpoints. These are the URLs that clients use to access resources, and they should be named with nouns, not verbs, such as `/users` or `/orders`. Using standard HTTP methods like GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE makes the API intuitive. It is also crucial to return appropriate status codes, like 200 for success, 404 for missing resources, and 500 for server errors. This helps developers understand what happened. Furthermore, thorough documentation is vital, as it guides users on how to make requests. Finally, always plan for versioning—for example, by adding a version number to the URL (like `/v1/users`)—so that future updates do not break existing clients. These practices lead to APIs that are reliable and developer-friendly.
